description: An additive oscillator: a sine fundamental with eight switchable overtones above it at harmonics two to nine, each at one over its harmonic number

params.text: Switches that overtone in or out of the sum; the lamp above it shows whether it is actually sounding once the filter and the mask CV have had their say
Keeps all the harmonics, only the odd-numbered ones, or only the even-numbered ones
Sets the pitch, four octaves either side of 261.63Hz, shown in hertz on the tooltip

inputs.text: Sets the pitch as a volt per octave, added to the frequency knob; the result is held between 8Hz and 20000Hz

Picks the set of overtones directly and takes the eight switches out of the picture: 0-10V is read as an eight-bit pattern by default, or as a count of harmonics from the bottom up on the menu setting
Picks the harmonic filter: below 1.67V all the harmonics, below 3.33V the odd ones only, and above that the even ones only, taking the panel switch out of the picture

outputs.text: The sum of the fundamental and whichever overtones are sounding, normalised to ±5V so that switching harmonics changes the timbre and not the level

notes: the fundamental is always present and cannot be switched out; the eight switches control the overtones above it
an overtone is switched in or out at its own next zero crossing rather than at once, and the level normalisation is slewed over about 5ms, so changes do not click
menu: Mask CV Mode — a label over the two choices below it, setting how the mask input is read
Binary (8-bit pattern) — reads the mask input as an eight-bit number, the lowest bit being the second harmonic and the highest the ninth, so each step of about 0.039V gives a different set
Sweep (0-8 harmonics) — reads the mask input as a count of overtones switched in from the bottom up, so a rising voltage brightens the tone smoothly

inputs.0:
1V per octave · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V.
inputs.1:
0 to 10V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.2:
0 to 5V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
